definition: Mental measurement is the assessment of psychological or mental characteristics using questionnaires made up of individual items. In this context, the accuracy of the measurement can be affected when some questionnaire items are left unanswered.

reasons: The packet does not define “mental measurement” as a general assessment of psychological or mental characteristics; it only discusses mental measurement questionnaires and missing-item handling.
The claim that the term specifically refers to questionnaires made up of individual items is not supported by the source text.
The statement about accuracy being affected when questionnaire items are left unanswered is supported in substance, but the overall definition includes additional unsupported generalization.

The packet does not explicitly support the definition’s claim that “mental measurement” is the assessment of “psychological or mental characteristics.” It only references “mental measurement questionnaires” and missing-item effects, without defining the term that way.

The packet does support the second sentence’s general point that incomplete or missing questionnaire items can influence/affect measurement accuracy (“Incomplete data are of particular important influence in mental measurement questionnaires” and the study compares methods for handling missing items).
